chain.label: Autopilot time-based desensitization schedule sized for 40-degree-flap approach speeds
chain.trigger: The 150-second desensitization period used by the Sperry SP-50 and SP-150 autopilots was originally optimized for approach airspeeds corresponding to a 40-degree-flap setting.

chain.label: Sperry Service Bulletins reducing desensitization to 105 seconds never incorporated
chain.trigger: The autopilot installed on the airplane had not been modified in accordance with changes specified in two Sperry Service Bulletins, SBs 21-1132-121 and 21-1132-122.

chain.label: Freezing fog, 100-foot overcast, RVR 1,400-1,800 feet requiring a CAT II coupled approach
chain.trigger: visibility 1/2 statute mile in freezing fog, ceiling overcast at 100 feet agl... RVR on runway 14R of 1,400 feet variable to 1,800 feet.

chain.label: Autopilot gain remained higher than design intent and commanded divergent pitch oscillations
chain.trigger: the autopilot's 150-second desensitization rate was too slow for the accident airplane's approach speed, resulting in divergent pitch deviations at a low altitude at a critical time during the approach.

caused_by.evidence: Calculations based on FDR data indicated that the accident airplane actually traveled this distance in about 100 seconds. As a result, during the approach, the autopilot sensitivity was consistently higher than its intended design value.
The changes outlined by these SBs were designed to reduce the time required for autopilot desensitization from 150 seconds to 105 seconds.

chain.label: Captain's visual acquisition of the runway environment delayed; sunglasses worn through the approach
chain.trigger: a lack of horizon cues and what he described as a 'low runway light intensity setting' delayed his visual acquisition of the runway environment, and he noted that he wore his sunglasses throughout the descent and approach until touchdown.

caused_by.evidence: The captain stated that the lead-in lights were faint... increasing the potential for visual illusions as a result of reduced visibility.

chain.label: Nose-down pitch excursion to -6 degrees and descent well below glideslope inside the middle marker
chain.trigger: the airplane continued to pitch down to about -6 degrees and descended well below the glideslope... coincident with a full-scale, below glideslope instrument deflection about 60 feet agl.

caused_by.evidence: the autopilot with the 150-second desensitization period responded to the disturbances by commanding oscillatory pitch changes that increased over time and resulted in significant deviations from the desired flightpath.

chain.label: Crew failed to monitor and react to the pitch deviation and excessive sink rate at decision height
chain.trigger: the flight crew did not react in a proper and timely manner to excessive pitch deviations and descent rates... as required by the CAT II procedures outlined in the American Airlines 727 Operating Manual.

caused_by.evidence: During this period, the flight engineer stated, 'ooh nose uh,' and the captain did not disengage the autopilot or take any action to adjust the pitch attitude.
He stated that he then concentrated his attention outside the cockpit to locate the runway environment.

chain.label: Approach continued to touchdown instead of the required missed approach
chain.trigger: The flight engineer stated that the captain did not call for a missed approach or advance the throttles to go-around power before impact.

caused_by.evidence: the flight crew did not react... by either initiating a go-around or adjusting the pitch attitude and thrust to ensure a successful landing
a ground proximity warning system (GPWS) aural 'sink rate' alert; and the flight engineer state, 'nose up, nose up.'

chain.label: Belated pull-up and power addition at about 80 feet insufficient to arrest the descent
chain.trigger: The captain immediately pitched the airplane up to about 6 degrees and added a substantial amount of power. These actions were not sufficient or timely enough to arrest the descent.

caused_by.evidence: the captain added power and pulled back on the control column to arrest the sink
the descent rate rapidly increased to about 1,900 feet per minute

chain.label: Airplane struck the ground 314 feet short of the runway 14R threshold, separating the main gear
chain.trigger: the airplane continued to descend until it impacted the ground 314 feet short of the runway threshold, resulting in the separation of the main landing gear.

caused_by.evidence: These actions were not sufficient or timely enough to arrest the descent
FDR data indicated a descent rate of 1,350 feet per minute... at the time of impact

chain.label: Airplane bounced, slid down the runway, and came to rest in the mud beside it
chain.trigger: The airplane then became airborne, touched down again on the runway, and then slid about 2,350 feet down the runway until coming to rest in an upright position in the mud about 250 feet to the right (west) of the runway.

caused_by.evidence: resulting in the separation of the main landing gear

chain.label: Twenty-two passengers and one flight attendant received minor injuries; airplane a hull loss
chain.trigger: Twenty-two passengers and one flight attendant reported that they received minor injuries during the accident and subsequent emergency evacuation.

caused_by.evidence: two passenger seat belt attachments became unhooked at impact for undetermined reasons, causing minor injuries to one passenger
An emergency evacuation was initiated after the airplane came to a complete stop... a ceiling stowage compartment door dropped down and blocked the forward entry door
